1:
1. Do not hold the handrails!
2. Keep your gaze forward.
3. Step from toe to heel.
4. Intervals (30 sec sprint + 60 sec walk) are more effective than steady-state running.
2:
1. Lie on an incline bench.
2. Lower the dumbbells to chest level, keeping a neutral wrist position.
3. Pause at the bottom.
4. Press the dumbbells in a slight arc toward each other at the top.
3:
1. Lie down, retract your shoulder blades, and keep a slight arch in your lower back (create a small bridge).
2. Lower the barbell to your mid-chest, keeping elbows at a 45° angle to your torso.
3. Press the bar up explosively.
4:
1. Stand straight, lean your torso slightly forward to protect your lower back.
2. Keep your elbows slightly bent.
3. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until parallel with the floor (lifting higher is not recommended to avoid shoulder injury).
5:
1. Inhale as you lower yourself until your elbows reach a 90° angle (or slightly deeper).
2. Exhale and press yourself up powerfully.
3. At the top, do not lock out your elbows.
4. Keep your shoulders down and back (avoid shrugging).
6:
1. Starting position: grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Fully extend your arms.
2. Pull up: exhale and pull yourself up, aiming to touch the bar with your upper chest.
3. Hold: pause at the top for 1 second, fully contracting your back muscles.
7:
1. Hang from the bar, slightly tilting your pelvis upward.
2. Exhale and raise your straight legs to parallel with the floor or higher.
3. Lower your legs slowly, over 2–3 seconds.
8:
1. Keep your elbows tightly fixed at your sides.
2. Move only your forearms, keeping your wrists straight.
3. Pause for 1 second at the top for peak contraction.
9:
1. Hinge forward with a straight back, press your working shoulder against your torso.
2. Exhale and fully extend your arm with the dumbbell backward.
3. Pause at the top and squeeze your tricep hard.
10:
1. Lie on a bench, extend your arms holding the barbell overhead.
2. Inhale and bend your elbows, lowering the bar to your forehead or behind your head (keep elbows pointing forward).
3. Exhale and extend your arms strictly at the elbow joints.
11:
1. Stand straight, holding the barbell across your upper back/shoulders.
2. Bend your knees, lowering your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Return to the starting position.
12:
1. Take a wide step forward.
2. Bend both knees to a 90° angle.
3. Push off with your front foot and return to the starting position.
13:
1. Stand straight, holding a barbell or dumbbells in front of you.
2. Slightly hinge forward, pushing your hips back.
3. Lower the weight along your legs to mid-shin level, keeping your back straight.
14:
1. Sit in the leg press machine.
2. Place your feet on the platform shoulder-width apart.
3. Release the safety handles, bend and extend your legs under full control, without locking your knees at the top.
15:
1. Sit in the machine, pressing your back firmly against the pad.
2. Extend your legs forward, fully contracting your quadriceps.
3. Slowly and controllably lower the weight back to the starting position.
16:
1. Lie or sit face down in the machine.
2. Bend your knees, pulling the roller as close to your glutes as possible.
3. Focus on contracting your hamstrings, controlling the movement.
17:
1. Stand with your toes on an elevated surface (step or weight plate), heels hanging off.
2. Lower your heels down to stretch your calves.
3. Rise onto your toes as high as possible, hold for a second.
18:
1. Place one foot toes-down on a bench behind you.
2. Squat down on your front leg until you reach a 90° knee angle.
3. Return to the starting position by straightening your front leg.
19:
1. Anchor the straps at the highest point (above head level).
2. Grab the handles, extend your arms forward, and step forward to create tension.
3. Inhale, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels, bend your elbows at 45° and lower your chest toward your hands.
4. Exhale and powerfully return to the starting position.
20:
1. Adjust the straps to mid-length (handle level at chest height).
2. Grab the handles, extend your arms, and lean back on straight legs, heels on the floor.
3. Exhale, bend your elbows, pull your chest to your hands, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
21:
1. Face the anchor point, grab the handles, and extend your arms forward.
2. Lean back to create tension in the straps.
3. Inhale, keep your back straight, bend your knees, and squat down to a 90° angle, pushing your hips back.
4. Exhale and return to the starting position.
22:
1. Secure your grip on the rope.
2. Pull yourself up using only arm and core strength.
3. Keep your legs relaxed and do not use them for momentum.
23:
1. Stand between the high pulleys of a crossover machine.
2. Grab the handles, keep your elbows slightly bent.
3. Exhale and bring your hands together in front of your chest, squeezing your muscles.
4. Slowly return your hands to the starting position.
24:
1. Lie with your lower back on a stability ball, feet flat on the floor at a 90° angle.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head.
3. Exhale and crunch your torso upward, fully contracting your abs.
4. Inhale and slowly lower back down.
25:
1. Step onto the machine, keep your torso upright.
2. Alternately press the pedals, simulating climbing stairs.
3. Control your pace and breathing, avoid leaning heavily on the handrails.
26:
1. Stand straight, grip the kettlebell with both hands.
2. Hinge forward slightly, push your hips back.
3. Use a powerful hip and glute drive to swing the kettlebell up to chest level.
4. Control the weight at the bottom, keeping your back straight.
27:
1. Hold the jump rope, adjust the length to your height.
2. Rotate the handles with your wrists, not your whole arms.
3. Perform rhythmic jumps on your toes, landing softly.
4. Keep your torso straight, gaze forward.
28:
1. Anchor the resistance band at face level.
2. Grab the handles, step back to create tension.
3. Exhale and pull the handles toward your temples, rotating your wrists outward and squeezing your shoulder blades.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
29:
1. Lie face down on a hyperextension bench, secure your feet under the pads.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or place them behind your head.
3. Exhale and extend your torso upward, engaging your glutes and lower back.
4. Avoid hyperextending your lower back, hold the top position for a second.
